Geographic focus:
    United States
Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [NO]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]
Synopsis:
    Fed Governor Waller is signaling a dovish lean, advocating to "give disinflation a chance" and dampening expectations for a September rate hike. Near-term focus shifts to the August jobs report as the key data catalyst. A separate inflation risk factor — record-high diesel prices — looms heading into winter, adding upside pressure to the inflation outlook.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES (directly addresses Fed rate expectations, inflation dynamics, and labor market data all of which are core drivers of US yields and market pricing)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 25 (Waller's tone actively pushes back against a September hike; diesel prices introduce a residual hawkish risk but are not the dominant narrative)
Probability of increase: 20%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 65 (Waller's "give disinflation a chance" framing strongly implies a preference to pause/hold in September)
Probability of holding: 65%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 15 (no explicit discussion of cuts; dovish tone leans toward holding, not cutting, at this stage)
Probability of decrease: 15%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -35 (moderately dovish — Waller's signal leans against hiking in September, though record diesel prices introduce a countervailing hawkish undercurrent that prevents a fully dovish read)
